what_was_proven: MEGA's API endpoint https://g.api.mega.co.nz/cs rejects ANONYMOUS folder-node fetches with error -15 (ESID).
This is a SESSION DEMAND, not a 'link missing' result. Error -9 is ENOENT ('Object (typically, node or user) not found'); we did NOT receive -9.
Therefore the supplied link's existence, expiry state and contents are ALL STILL UNVERIFIED. Nothing about the corpus is known.

evidence.error_description_verbatim: Invalid or expired user session, please relogin
evidence.source_of_error_meaning: mega/errors.py _CODE_TO_DESCRIPTIONS, -15: ('ESID', 'Invalid or expired user session, please relogin')
evidence.byte_error_description_verbatim: Object (typically, node or user) not found
evidence.why_the_distinction_matters: -9 would have meant the node or link is absent. -15 means the API never got that far: it demanded credentials first. Conflating them would produce the documented retracted conclusion 'there is no download, the corpus is video-only' - a large wrong conclusion reached from the wrong layer.

variant_note: All five are the documented node-fetch shapes. All returned HTTP 200 with an in-band error code -15. HTTP 200 is not a receipt - this is acquisition-backends.md's 'soft-404' lesson applied to a JSON API: the discriminating power lives in the body, not the status line.
